title: AI detectors are creating a new era of distrust
summary: AI detection tools designed to identify AI-generated content are raising new trust concerns in educational and professional settings, mirroring longstanding problems with anti-plagiarism software. These detectors frequently produce false positives and may discourage legitimate AI use, creating tension between educators, students, and writers. The proliferation of AI detectors highlights broader questions about verifying authorship in an AI-driven world.
content:

How it started
Long before ChatGPT became a thing, educators and editors frequently used anti-plagiarism tools to see if writers were being honest about their work. These tools work by comparing a written work against a database filled with content from across the web, scholarly articles, and more to check for matching sentences and phrases. title: Mount Toba eruption doesn't seem like it could nearly kill our species
summary: New research challenges the widely accepted theory that the massive Mount Toba eruption nearly drove humanity to extinction. Evidence suggests the volcano had significantly less climate impact than previously believed, contradicting earlier catastrophe scenarios. This finding reshapes understanding of ancient climate disasters and human resilience to natural catastrophes.
content: The massive Toba eruption seems to have had little climate impact.

zh.title: 托巴火山喷发似乎不太可能几乎摧毁我们的物种
zh.summary: 新的研究挑战了广泛接受的理论，即托巴大规模火山喷发几乎将人类推向灭绝。证据表明该火山对气候的影响远低于之前的预期，与早期的灾难情景相矛盾。这一发现重塑了人们对古代气候灾难和人类对自然灾害抵御能力的理解。
